description:
ENGLISH:

Solo maker from Ankara, Turkey. Building a 1-meter tall, fully 3D printed Artemis SLS as a Young Astronaut Mission Training Vehicle. 10 parts, 5kg PLA, 200+ hours print. Designed for hands-on STEM education. Aligned with NASA's new 2027 Artemis 3 Earth-orbit docking mission. Includes 3 mission cards: Launch, Orbit, Rendezvous. Goal: To bring Artemis to classrooms in Ankara and make space tangible for kids. One person, one rocket, one big dream.
summary:
Our project is a fun and creative 3D model that shows how humans can build a new life on Mars in the future. Mars is a very cold, dry, and dusty planet. It has no air to breathe and no liquid water on the surface. To live there, we need oxygen, water, food, energy, and a very safe home. We designed a Mars Base that solves all of these problems.
Our model has strong dome houses for astronauts to live and sleep in, big solar panels to make clean energy from the Sun, large water tanks to store water, and a greenhouse to grow fresh vegetables and fruits. We also added a laboratory for science experiments, a control center to talk with Earth, a landing pad for rockets, and exploration vehicles to discover new places on Mars. All the buildings are connected with safe tunnels and roads.
We designed our 3D model on the computer and made a short video to show how our base works every day, from morning to night. We learned how astronauts live, work, eat, and stay safe in space. We also learned how to work as a team, solve problems, and turn our ideas into a real design.
This project helped us understand the challenges of living in space and combine STEM, design, and imagination. Our goal is to inspire kids who will live on Mars in the future and show that space is for everyone!
details: I made this project all by myself.My project is a 3D designed reusable rocket.I designed the rocket myself. Then I printed it all by myself with my 3D printer. It took 55 hours. I printed it piece by piece.After I came home from school, I did my homework first. Then I worked on my project. I assembled all the pieces myself.What does it do? My rocket carries satellites and scientific materials from Earth to space. After finishing its mission, it returns to Earth and can be used again. This saves both money and materials.How does it work? The rocket rises by using its fuel efficiently, leaves its load in space, and then returns to Earth in a controlled way with the help of a parachute and engine.What are its benefits? It makes going to space cheaper and more environmentally friendly. Scientists can send their experiments to space more easily.What tools did I use? I used my 3D printer and 3D modelling applications to design and build my rocket.. I did everything by myself.
